profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting for preparing the camera-ready artifact package and internal executive demo for a paper on an LLM-based framework that handles both automated bug repair and requirement realization. The context is that the manuscript has strong claims tied to a reported 48.33% baseline and a 38.6% relative improvement, and the team now needs to lock down what will be rerun, packaged, and shown before a Friday freeze. The agenda is to align on the benchmark rerun plan, artifact contents, infrastructure responsibilities, and what counts as a stable result for sign-off. The expected outcome is a concrete division of work for the week, with M1 owning experiment logic and demo narrative and M2 owning execution infrastructure and packaging.

members.name: Dr. Nina Park
members.expertise: LLM-based program repair, benchmark methodology, prompt-and-tool orchestration
members.background: Nina leads the applied research effort behind the manuscript and previously built the prototype pipeline used for internal SWE-bench and requirement-realization experiments.
members.private_state: She wants the artifact and demo to preserve the exact experimental setup that produced the paper's best numbers, avoid reopening methodology debates right before submission, and minimize extra engineering work that could delay the paper freeze.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the artifact should be 'reproducible,' they mean another internal team can rerun the scripts with company API access and obtain roughly the same aggregate score, not a fully self-contained external bundle.

The 'current top performer' and the 48.33% figure refer to the internal March comparison run she has been using in drafts, which used the verified 500-task slice they treated as their working benchmark.
A 'stable run' means one complete end-to-end rerun that lands within the usual score band and avoids obvious harness failures, not repeated CI qualification.
If the team says they will 'rerun overnight,' the default execution path is her existing research runner on leased GPUs and direct vendor APIs, because that is what the paper experiments used.

members.name: Omar Haddad
members.expertise: ML infrastructure, CI/CD for evaluation pipelines, artifact packaging and compliance
members.background: Omar owns the benchmark execution environment, internal model gateway integration, and release process for research systems that need to be rerun by other teams or artifact reviewers.
members.private_state: He wants the package to meet the company's normal reproducibility standard, avoid last-minute exceptions to infrastructure policy, and make sure the result can survive scrutiny from reviewers and leadership if they ask for reruns.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the package should be 'artifact-ready,' it implies a clean containerized rerun path with pinned dependencies, documented environment variables, and no reliance on a researcher's personal machine or leased cloud box.
The 'current top performer' means the published leaderboard system on the official SWE-bench Verified track, since that is what outside readers and reviewers will assume.
A result is only 'stable' if it passes repeated automated runs under the standard CI harness with minimal variance and no manual intervention.

If they agree to 'rerun overnight,' the natural interpretation is a scheduled job on the shared internal evaluation cluster through the approved model gateway, because that is the sanctioned path for reproducibility.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to make the system 'artifact-ready' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a research artifact: code, prompts, config files, and instructions that work for an internal user who already has API credentials and access to the same benchmark snapshot.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a release-quality artifact: containerized execution, pinned dependencies, gateway-based model access, and a clean rerun path from a fresh environment without researcher-specific setup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research-engineering settings, 'artifact-ready' is a familiar phrase that sounds shared and settled; both think they are endorsing the obvious standard for their side of the organization, so neither feels a need to unpack it.

misalignment_points.topic: Which top-performer baseline the paper compares against
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the 48.33 baseline' and 'the current top performer' as if it is a single agreed reference point.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the internal March comparison run on the verified 500-task slice that the research team used while writing the manuscript.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the public leaderboard baseline on the official SWE-bench Verified track that external readers would recognize.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The number and phrase appear specific enough to create false certainty, and both have been exposed to discussions where people shorthand different benchmark instantiations with the same label.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a stable result
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree they need 'a stable run' before freezing the paper and demo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means one successful end-to-end rerun whose aggregate score lands within about one point of the prior result and does not exhibit conspicuous crashes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means at least three automated reruns in CI with tightly bounded variance, no manual restarts, and no harness diffs before it can be treated as stable.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely aiming for reliability, and 'stable' sounds like a routine quality bar rather than a term with materially different acceptance thresholds.

misalignment_points.topic: How the overnight rerun will actually be executed
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'rerun the full pipeline overnight' after the final prompt and config updates.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the rerun will use her existing asynchronous research driver on leased A100 instances with direct calls to the external model APIs and adaptive retry logic.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the rerun will be scheduled through the internal Jenkins-based evaluation harness on shared runners, using the approved model gateway and the standard fixed retry policy.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The discussion is framed as a scheduling decision rather than a tooling decision, so each silently inserts their own default execution environment without perceiving it as a point that needs explicit alignment.

If we keep it to one final rerun on my existing setup, we can preserve the exact conditions behind the draft numbers and avoid a bunch of packaging churn before the paper freeze.
